text:
carla: Heads up 02 invoice from TelTek Ltd (IL) came in with 17% Israeli VAT charged. Sales say the work was delivered remotely to Redwood Ltd (UK). Can tax confirm whether reverse-charge or export of services applies and what we should ask the vendor?

carla: Invoice snapshot:
```
INV-IL-2026-078
Vendor: TelTek Ltd, VAT IL512345678
Billed to: Redwood Ltd (UK)
Description: SaaS integration and remote engineering support (Mar 2026)
Net: \u20ac8,500
VAT (17% Israel): \u20ac1,445
Total: \u20ac9,945
```

sarah: Tax team here. Israel VAT (17%) generally applies to taxable supplies in Israel. However, for services provided to a foreign business, Israeli law may treat certain services as exported and zero-rated if the supplier can substantiate the export. Important: VIES doesn't cover Israel, so we can't rely on that. We need: vendors Israeli VAT registration, a written statement that services were performed outside Israel (dates + personnel), and evidence that the customer is a business (buyer VAT/GST/registration).

ori-vendor: Hi all  Ori from TelTek. We invoiced with VAT because our accounting team uses an automatic VAT rule. We are registered in Israel: VAT IL512345678. We can provide a signed declaration that work was performed for Redwood UK personnel and all activity was executed remotely from Israel. What exact wording/evidence do you need?

mike: Sales confirms the PO and onboarding note reference Redwood Ltd (UK) and the contact is the London account team. I'll attach the PO.

invoicebot: INV-IL-2026-078 uploaded to NetSuite. Status: HOLD_TAX_DISCREPANCY.

sarah: Ideal package from vendor: (1) Reissued invoice without Israeli VAT showing buyer registration (UK VAT GB999888777) and referencing the export or reverse charge rule; OR (2) Signed export-of-services statement including vendor VAT, vendor address, statement of where services were performed, and a note that this supply should be zero-rated under Israeli VAT export rules. Either works for audit, but reissue is cleaner. If vendor can't reissue, finance can pay gross and well attempt to reclaim through Redwood Ltd VAT return, but that is admin-heavy and slower.

ori-vendor: We can issue (2) immediately  a signed statement detailing personnel, dates, and that services were supplied to a UK VAT-registered business, plus our VAT certificate. Will that let you clear the hold?

carla: That should be fine. @sarah will confirm, but we need the UK VAT for Redwood Ltd and a copy of the PO. Please add wording: "This invoice relates to exported services to a business customer in the UK and is zero-rated for Israeli VAT purposes per Israeli VAT law; TelTek Ltd VAT registration IL512345678." Signed and dated.

sarah: Yes  with that package we can clear the hold: (a) vendor signed statement, (b) copy of TelTek Israeli VAT certificate, (c) buyer business evidence (UK VAT GB999888777 or equivalent). Finance will attach these to the NetSuite invoice for VAT audit trail. If vendor reissues a corrected invoice showing zero VAT and buyer VAT, even better.

ori-vendor: Understood. We'll send a signed statement + VAT cert and can reissue a zero-VAT invoice referencing the buyer VAT. Expect both in the next 24h.

mike: Thanks  Ill forward PO and buyer VAT to Ori.

carla: Finance note: once we have the vendor docs, match to PO, update supplier ledger, remove HOLD_TAX_DISCREPANCY, and store documents in /finance/vat-audit/2026/teltek.

sarah: Also tagging for records: if TelTek later claims input VAT credit in Israel, we'll need the same docs; keep copies.

carla: Closing when documents arrive. :white_check_mark:
